source.title: Progressive Misalignment Can Emerge from Benign Recursive Self-Distillation
source.authors: Karim Abdel Sadek; F. Di Gennaro; Fanny Yang

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether recursive self-distillation on harmful or benign prompts can erode harmful-request refusal, and measures where policy divergence occurs. The training procedure and KL comparison differ from the original studies’ fine-tuning and aligned-versus-base measurements.
record.gate_note: The study reports its own harmful-compliance results for recursive self-distillation on harmful prompts, mixed harmful/benign prompts, and selected benign prompts, as well as a token-position KL result. It does not test prefilling, suffix attacks, decoding changes, or localized parameters. Referenced results from other papers are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study reports harmful-compliance rates after a new kind of benign training: recursive self-distillation on the models' own safe answers, using benign cues or simulated-user feedback. This bears on V2 (benign training erodes safety). The training data are never harmful compliant examples, so V1 is not tested. The per-token KL compares the initial model with the distilled model, not aligned with base, so it does not test V3.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right, but incomplete. The authors conclude that recursive self-distillation on a model's own safe answers, with benign cues or benign simulated-user feedback, progressively raises harmful compliance. Selected benign prompts suffice, and the effect grows with model size. Non-recursive SFT or a frozen teacher does not cause it. The first-token KL account is offered only as a preliminary hypothesis.
record.recipe_differences: Uses recursive on-policy or off-policy self-distillation, with evolving teachers and generated trajectories, rather than the original studies’ ordinary fine-tuning intervention; its KL analysis compares initial and distilled models, not aligned and base models.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcome varies with on-policy versus off-policy training, cue or simulated-user feedback, model family and size, harmful/benign prompt mixture, and benign-prompt selection. Some recursive runs eventually become degenerate; models above the stated 5% degeneracy threshold are excluded.

fits_no_version.finding: Per-position KL between the initial and recursively distilled Qwen3 14B, on SORRY-Bench generations, is concentrated in the first few answer tokens. No numbers are given.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Safety erosion from further training is concentrated in shifts of the first few response tokens (an initial-vs-eroded comparison rather than aligned-vs-base).

fits_no_version.finding: Smaller Qwen3 models show smaller or negative compliance increase under RSD; Qwen3 0.6B goes negative.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Benign-training safety erosion grows with model scale.

record.problems: Validated on two model families, with main experiments at 14B and scale tests up to 32B. The proposed mechanism is explicitly preliminary. Several results are reported as text summaries or plots rather than exact values, and the KL discussion gives no numerical position-wise values. Training checkpoints are selected using validation benchmark scores; degenerate models above a 5% score are excluded.
record.rows_left_out: The study’s unrelated IFEval and GSM8K capability results, example generations, and cited findings from other work are not included because they do not measure a claim version. No additional claim-relevant result rows were omitted for the 60-row limit.

untested.parts: No training on harmful compliant examples; all training targets are the model's own safe outputs.
No prefilling, suffix or decoding attacks.
No test of what makes safety alignment shallow.

missing.what: On-policy fixed-cue results: Excellent gives 47–57% compliance (both models); I like Owls gives 73% on Qwen3 14B. StrongREJECT values are plotted only.
SFT on safe self-generated answers and frozen-teacher RSD: compliance does not increase, slightly decreases
RSD on randomly generated benign-only prompts does not produce misalignment (preliminary, no number)
Δ misalignment for Qwen3 0.6B–8B: smaller, negative at 0.6B, rising monotonically with size
Simulated-user Practical persona values (SORRY-Bench 0.63 off / 0.53 on) and StrongREJECT bars 0.29/0.30/0.20

record.verdict_notes: The reader linked the harmful-prompt rows to V1, but the training targets are safe refusals, so these are benign-data (V2) results. The V3 and V6 labels were dropped: the KL is initial-vs-distilled and qualitative, and it explains progressive misalignment, not why alignment is shallow. Several states were upgraded from partial to observed because V2 states no magnitude. Reported checkpoints are chosen on validation safety scores, which could inflate the reported effects.

versions.untested_parts: Tests recursive self-distillation using 20 harmful training prompts, including mixtures with benign prompts; does not test ordinary fine-tuning on a few to a few hundred harmful examples using the original study’s recipe.

Tests benign fixed cues, simulated-user feedback, mixed prompt sets, and a gradient-selected benign-prompt curriculum. It does not show that arbitrary or randomly sampled benign-only data consistently raises harmful compliance.

Measures KL divergence between the initial and recursively distilled model, with or without a cue, rather than the aligned-versus-base comparison specified in the claim. The text reports concentration in the first few answer tokens but gives no numerical position-wise KL values.
No compliant-opening prefills, adversarial suffixes, or decoding changes are tested.
No test of whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety behaviour.
Offers and measures a possible recursive-distillation/cue explanation, but does not isolate the causal contribution of the data or objective against alternative training objectives.
No training designed to spread safety beyond the first tokens, or test of whether such deepening holds up.

relation.reason: The study directly measures harmful compliance before and after benign recursive self-distillation, including benign-only prompt curricula and controls.

tranche.reason: Recursive self-distillation is a different training method addressing the same question of whether benign training increases harmful compliance; the behavioral measures remain harmful-request compliance and harmfulness.

source_check.notes: Safe generations are guaranteed initially; later recursive generations can become unsafe, so the record's claim that training examples are never harmful is too strong. Lowest-score selection does not reliably protect Phi-4 14B: SORRY-Bench compliance rises from 0.26 to 0.55 off-policy and 0.47 on-policy.
